at trænge.explanation: "At trænge" means "to need / push through". To say something forces its way in, say: "Vandet trænger ind" (The water gets in). To say you really need something, add "til" (for): "Jeg trænger til ferie" (I really need a vacation).

at trøste.explanation: "At trøste" means "to comfort". To say how you comfort someone, add "med" (with): "Hun trøster ham med et kram" (She comforts him with a hug).

at tude.explanation: "At tude" means "to cry / howl". To tell a child to stop crying loudly, say: "Hold op med at tude!" (Stop bawling!) To say a siren makes a long loud sound, say: "Sirenen tuder" (The siren is wailing). It is an informal word.

at tvivle.explanation: "At tvivle" means "to doubt". To say what you doubt, add "på" (on): "Jeg tvivler på, at han kommer" (I doubt that he is coming).

at tvivle på.explanation: "At tvivle på" means "to doubt". To say you doubt that something will happen, start the second part with "at" (that): "Jeg tvivler på, at han kommer" (I doubt that he is coming). To say you are unsure, use "at være i tvivl" (to be in doubt): "Jeg er i tvivl" (I am unsure).

at tyde.explanation: "At tyde" means "to interpret". To ask someone to read old handwriting, say: "Kan du tyde det gamle brev?" (Can you interpret the old letter?) Do not mix it up with "at tyde på" (to suggest / indicate). To say the signs point to something, say: "Det tyder på regn" (It suggests rain).

at tyde på.explanation: "At tyde på" means "to suggest / indicate". To say the signs lead to a conclusion, say: "Alt tyder på, at det bliver koldt" (Everything suggests that it will be cold). Do not mix it up with "at tyde" (to interpret), which has no "på" (on). To say you read hard writing, say: "Jeg tyder skriften" (I interpret the writing).

at tygge.explanation: "At tygge" means "to chew". To name what you chew on, add "på" (on): "Hunden tygger på en pind" (The dog chews on a stick). The word "tyggegummi" (chewing gum) is built from "at tygge" (to chew) and "gummi" (rubber).

at tåle.explanation: "At tåle" means "to tolerate / stand". To say you cannot stand something, use it with "ikke" (not): "Jeg tåler ikke larm" (I cannot stand noise). To say a material can take something, say: "Tøjet tåler vask" (The clothes can take washing).

at tælle.explanation: "At tælle" means "to count". Its past forms "jeg talte" (I counted) and "jeg har talt" (I have counted) are the same as the past forms of "at tale" (to speak). To say you counted, say: "Jeg talte pengene" (I counted the money). To say you spoke, say: "Vi talte hele natten" (We talked all night).

at tænde.explanation: "At tænde" means "to turn on". To say you light a candle or a fire, use it too: "Vi tænder bålet" (We light the fire). To say you turn on a TV, a radio or running water, add "for" (for): "Jeg tænder for radioen" (I turn on the radio).

at tænde for.explanation: "At tænde for" means "to turn on". To say you turn on a radio, a TV or the water, add "for" (for): "Jeg tænder for radioen" (I turn on the radio). To say you turn on a light, use "at tænde" (to turn on, to light): "Jeg tænder lyset" (I turn on the light).

at tænke.explanation: "At tænke" means "to think". To say someone is on your mind, add "på" (of): "Jeg tænker på dig" (I am thinking of you). To give an opinion, use "at synes" (to think, to have an opinion): "Jeg synes, det er godt" (I think it is good).

at tænke over.explanation: "At tænke over" means "to think about". To say you are thinking a matter over, say: "Jeg tænker over det" (I am thinking it over). To say someone is on your mind, use "at tænke på" (to think of): "Jeg tænker på dig" (I am thinking of you).

at tænke på.explanation: "At tænke på" means "to think of". To say a person is on your mind, say: "Jeg tænker på min mor" (I am thinking of my mother). To say you are thinking a matter over, use "at tænke over" (to think about): "Jeg tænker over det" (I am thinking it over).

at tænke sig om.explanation: "At tænke sig om" means "to think carefully". The word "sig" (oneself) changes with who is thinking: "jeg tænker mig om" (I think carefully), "han tænker sig om" (he thinks carefully).

at tø.explanation: "At tø" means "to thaw". To say it is thawing, start with "det" (it): "Det tør" (It is thawing). The same spelling "tør" is also the word for "dry": "tør hud" (dry skin). It is also the word for "dare": "Jeg tør ikke" (I do not dare).

at tømme.explanation: "At tømme" means "to empty". The adjective "tom" (empty) is the related word, so "at tømme" makes something "tom". To say you empty a bin, say: "Jeg tømmer skraldespanden" (I empty the trash can).

at tørre.explanation: "At tørre" means "to dry". To say something loses its water, say: "Tøjet tørrer hurtigt" (The clothes dry quickly). To say you wipe a surface, add "af" (off): "Jeg tørrer bordet af" (I wipe the table off).

at tørre af.explanation: "At tørre af" means "to wipe / dry (dishes)". To say you wipe a table, say: "Han tørrer bordet af" (He wipes the table). To say you dry plates, say: "Hun tørrer tallerkenerne af" (She dries the plates). To mop up a spill, use "at tørre op" (to wipe up): "Jeg tørrer vandet op" (I wipe up the water).

at tørre støv af.explanation: "At tørre støv af" means "to dust". It is built from "at tørre" (to wipe), "støv" (dust) and "af" (off). To say how often someone dusts, put "af" (off) at the end: "Han tørrer støv af hver uge" (He dusts every week).

en t-shirt.explanation: "En t-shirt" means "a t-shirt". To say you wear one, use "at have" (to have) with "på" (on): "Jeg har en t-shirt på" (I am wearing a t-shirt). Literally, it is "I have a t-shirt on".

en tabel.explanation: "En tabel" means "a table", as in rows and columns of information. To say the piece of furniture, use "et bord" (a table): "Bogen ligger på bordet" (The book is on the table).

en tablet.explanation: "En tablet" means "a tablet", as in the flat touchscreen computer. To say a pill, use the same word: "Jeg tager en tablet mod smerter" (I take a pill for pain).
